newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dollar steady, bonds seesaw on data.
newsitem.headline: Australia dollar steady, bonds seesaw on data.

text.p: The Australian dollar was steady while bonds seesawed around the time of release of the Department of Industrial Relations report on enterprise bargaining agreements which showed moderation in wages growth.

The local dollar held around US$0.8110/15, while the December 10-year bond futures contract rose to 92.890 from 92.855 just before the official 10.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) release time of the report then slipped back to 92.865.

Average annualised wages based on wage agreements covering almost 200,000 employees rose 4.8 percent in the September quarter, down from a revised 5.3 percent in the previous quarter, the report said.
It also said private sector wages rose an average 5.3 percent in the September quarter, down from a revised 6.1 percent previously.

The Reserve Bank expressed concerns over wages growth through enterprise bargaining agreements in last month's quarterly Bulletin, saying that the recent moderation in aggregate wages might not be sustained.
